metadata.name: nice
metadata.displayName: nice - Run a program with modified priority
metadata.description: Run a command with a specified nice value (scheduling priority)

installation.note: nice is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: The nice command runs another command with an adjusted scheduling priority (nice value). Lower priority (higher nice value) means the process is "nicer" to other processes and gets less CPU time. Useful for running non-critical tasks in the background without impacting interactive or critical workloads.
when_to_use: Run a long batch job with lower priority so it does not slow the system
Start a backup or build with reduced CPU contention
Run non-urgent tasks so interactive use stays responsive

syntax.description: If no COMMAND is given, nice prints the current default nice value. With a command, it runs that command with an adjusted nice value.

options.description: Add ADJUSTMENT to the nice value (default 10). Range is typically -20 (highest priority) to 19 (lowest).
options.use_case: Set a specific nice value; 19 is common for low-priority background work

examples.title: Run a script with lowest priority
examples.description: Run the script with nice value 19 so it uses CPU only when others are idle
examples.use_case: Background tasks that should not affect interactive use

examples.title: Run make with slightly lower priority
examples.description: Build with a modest priority reduction
examples.use_case: Compilation that should not starve other processes

common_pitfalls.description: Only root can use negative nice values (e.g., nice -n -5) to give higher priority.
common_pitfalls.solution: Regular users can only lower priority (positive nice or default). Use sudo for negative nice if permitted by policy.

related_commands.description: Change the nice value of an already-running process
Shows NI (nice) column for running processes
